html:
An Italian Dominican friar and the most influential theologian of the Latin Middle Ages. He was born around 1225 near Aquino, to a noble family that sent him to school at Monte Cassino and hoped he would become its abbot.

Instead he joined the new Dominican order of preaching friars. His family seized him and kept him at home for about a year, but he did not give in. He taught at the University of Paris and in Italy.

His great project was to show that faith and reason do not conflict. The works of Aristotle, newly translated into Latin along with the commentaries of Averroes, had excited and alarmed Christian scholars. Aquinas used Aristotle's logic and philosophy to build a full system of Christian teaching in his Summa Theologica. It includes his "five ways" of proving that God exists.

Some of his ideas were condemned in Paris in 1277, after his death, but he was made a saint in 1323. His thought, Thomism, became the basis of Catholic teaching. Dante placed him in Paradise.
